Alex: quick sync — ran a 6h replay against a 2% sample of prod traces (cohort=interactive). noticing kernel selection flips between runs
Cheng: what does "flips" mean here? different kernel ids for same request?
Alex: yes, same request seq -> sometimes kernel_v1 sometimes kernel_v3. perf delta ~5% avg token cost.
Marta: are we sure the selector is deterministic? we sort by score but if score ties use map iteration right?
Alex: seems like that. also saw KV cache warmup variance across runs which amplifies tail.
Sam: can you share the exact harness command you ran?
Alex: pasted below:
```
./replay_harness \
  --trace-dir s3://redwood-prod-traces/2026/03/ \
  --cohort interactive \
  --sample-rate 0.02 \
  --anonymize cohort_id \
  --seed 0 \
  --kv-warmup-mode prefix --profile flame
```
Cheng: two quick hypotheses: (1) kernel tie-breaker non-determinism because of unordered map; (2) kernel scoring uses a timestamp metric that isn't scrubbed by anonymize.
Marta: +1 on unordered map. we used a map for kernel candidate buckets in selector. fix = stable sort on (score, kernel_name) in selection path.
Alex: I patched selector to stable sort, re-ran same sample with seed=0, seed=1, seed=2. kernel flip rate dropped from ~18% to ~0.7%. perf spread reduced to ~0.4%.
Sam: nice. what about KV behavior? still noisy?
Alex: KV cache still has run-to-run variance in p99 latency on cold cohorts. suspect we warmup different prefixes depending on sampling order.
QA-Sim: infra note — sampling order is deterministic given seed, but our cohort sampler groups by user id hash which depends on anonymization salt. if anonymize changes, order changes.
Marta: maybe we need a two-stage anonymize: stable cohort id + ephemeral token scrub. keep sampling order stable across runs.
Alex: trying synthetic alignment experiment: force identical batch boundaries and pre-warm KV with replay of prefix-only traces. command snippet:
```
./replay_harness --trace-dir s3://... --seed 42 --force-batch-boundary --prewarm-prefixes s3://prefixes/interactive-10k.json
```
Sam: if we force batch boundaries we can compare apples-to-apples on batching heuristics. good idea.
Cheng: profiler output (flame) shows kernel_v3 memcpy + data-layout copy hot path on these traces. that explains perf delta when kernel_v3 chosen.
Alex: flame link: https://internal-grafana/replay/flames/2249999999 (private)
Marta: was kernel_v3 a patched build? maybe the new layout optimization regressed memmove pattern.
Alex: kernel_v3 was rolled last week (quant conv reorder). revert candidate reduces p99 by 120ms in synthetic run.
DeployBot: canary deploy: kernel_v3 -> kernel_v2 on pool inference-dedicated-4 scheduled in 30m.
Sam: plan: (1) land deterministic stable-sort in selector; (2) add replay harness flags to force batch boundaries + prefix prewarm; (3) add parity checks to CI: run 3 seeds, confirm token-level edit distance == 0 for functional parity and perf delta < 0.5% for economics parity; (4) add kernel smoke (repro) job to nightly for top 5 cohorts.
Cheng: parity check details: compute per-request token diff and also per-token latency distribution. flag if >0 token diffs OR perf p95 change > 0.5%. small delta tolerance for quant rounding (we use edit-distance threshold 1e-3).
QA-Sim: I'll add anonymization stability tests: ensure cohort hash salt is pinned for replay suite and recorded in trace metadata.
Marta: also add a test for KV warmup determinism: prewarm script should run before perf capture. mark the metric capture window after N prewarm tokens.
Alex: FYI: found one more noise source — dynamic kernel selection uses runtime free_gpu_memory measure. that metric fluctuates slightly per run due to background housekeeping. we should snap that metric at harness start or use historical avg.
Sam: good catch. we should decouple selection signal from ephemeral noise in one mode ("replay-stable").
Marta: ok I'll draft a small RFC for "replay-stable" mode (stable selectors, pinned salts, forced batch boundaries, prewarm).
Alex: results after stable-sort + prewarm: token cost variance -> 0.3% across seeds; kernel choices stable > 99%. p99 tail decreased 80ms.
Cheng: recommend we add these steps to the perf regression playbook and make a small CI job that runs against a ~1k trace sample nightly.
Sam: 👍 I'll add task to eng-runtime sprint board.
InfraBot: loadtest started: replay-suite/nightly/2249999999 (tracking id rps-2249)
Alex: thanks all. next step: Marta to RFC, Sam to CI job, QA-Sim to add anonymize tests.
Marta: I'll post RFC draft in #eng-runtime tomorrow. :thumbsup:
QA-Sim: will follow up with small harness config PR.
Sam: closing loop — good win on reducing noise floor. :rocket:
